aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer, defined as Gleason score 7-10.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: There were 1739 total and 489 high-grade (Gleason 7-10) PCa cases and 3117 men in the randomly selected cohort.
study_design: Prospective case-cohort analysis within the Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial.
reason: The abstract analyzes both total incident prostate cancer and high-grade incident prostate cancer. The 3117 figure is the randomly selected subcohort rather than a clearly stated total analytic participant count.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Selenium supplementation (combined selenium only and selenium + vitamin E arms) had no effect among men with low selenium status (<60th percentile of toenail selenium) but increased the risk of high-grade PCa among men with higher selenium status by 91% (P = .007).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns high-grade prostate cancer among men with higher baseline selenium status.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Vitamin E supplementation (alone) had no effect among men with high selenium status (≥40th percentile of toenail selenium) but increased the risks of total, low-grade, and high-grade PCa among men with lower selenium status (63%, P = .02; 46%, P = .09; 111%, P = .008, respectively).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's 63% increase and 1739-case count correspond to total prostate cancer, the first endpoint reported in the respective sequence.
